questions.q: What does a Lead object represent?
options: A person or company that might become a customer, but hasn't been qualified yet
A company that has already been a paying customer for years
A confirmed, in-progress deal
A support ticket from an existing customer
questions.explain: A Lead is an unqualified prospect — a raw inquiry before it's proven to be real.

questions.q: Why does Salesforce keep Leads as a separate object instead of creating an Account, Contact, and Opportunity for every inquiry immediately?
options: To keep unproven, unqualified prospects out of the real pipeline data that sales reports on
To make cold-calling slower for sales reps
Because Leads are technically identical to Opportunities
Because Salesforce doesn't allow more than one object per record
questions.explain: Separating Leads prevents inflating real pipeline numbers with contacts that may never convert.

questions.q: Which Lead field tracks where a Lead originally came from (Web, Trade Show, Referral, etc.), and drives most marketing-attribution analysis?
options: Status
Rating
Amount
Lead Source
questions.explain: Lead Source records the origin channel and is the field behind channel-performance and attribution analysis.

options: Merges the Lead into an existing Case
Permanently deletes the Lead record and all its data
Creates an Account and a Contact (and usually an Opportunity) from the Lead's data, while marking the original Lead as Converted
Changes the Lead's Rating to Hot automatically
questions.explain: Conversion creates linked Account/Contact/Opportunity records; the original Lead is marked Converted, not deleted.

questions.q: After Lead Conversion, where does the analytical trail for "which marketing channel produced this deal" live?
options: It requires tracing from the converted Lead's Lead Source through to the resulting Opportunity, since the two are separate but linked objects
It's lost permanently once conversion happens
Entirely on the Contact record's Rating field
Entirely and only on the Opportunity record, with no connection back to the original Lead
questions.explain: The original Lead Source lives on the converted Lead record; the ongoing sales activity lives on the Opportunity — connected by the conversion link.
